title: Average of the Last K Readings
statement:
Readings from a sensor arrive one at a time. Build a class that reports the average of the most recent size readings after each one arrives.

  • MovingAverage(size) sets the window size.
  • next(val) records the reading val and returns the average of the last size readings, including this one. While fewer than size readings have arrived, it averages all of them so far.

Answers within 10⁻⁵ of the exact value are accepted. Tests are a list of operations and their arguments; the first creates the object, and the expected output has one entry per operation (null for the constructor).

examples.why: Until three readings exist, divide by how many there are. The last call drops the 1: (10 + 3 + 5) / 3 = 6.
A window of one always reports just the latest reading.

hints: Recomputing the sum of the window on every call costs O(size). What changes between two consecutive windows?
Exactly one reading enters, and once the window is full, exactly one reading leaves: the oldest one.
Keep the readings in a queue and a running sum. Add the new reading; if the queue is longer than size, subtract and remove the oldest. Divide by the queue length.

explain.intuition:
Each new window is the previous one plus the new reading, minus the oldest reading once the window is full. So a running sum can be updated with one addition and at most one subtraction, instead of adding up the whole window again.

To know which reading leaves, keep the readings in arrival order: a queue, or a ring buffer of length size where the slot you are about to overwrite holds exactly the reading that leaves. It is the same bookkeeping as an FPS counter that averages the last few frame times.
steps: Keep a ring buffer of size slots, a write position, a count of readings so far, and a running sum.
On next(val), if the buffer is full, subtract the value in the slot about to be overwritten.
Write val into that slot, add it to sum, advance the position and the count (capped at size).
pitfalls: Dividing by size before the window has filled up. The first call with size = 3 must return the reading itself, not a third of it.
Integer division in languages that have it. The average of 1 and 2 is 1.5.
Re-summing the whole window each call. It works, but turns a constant-time update into O(size).

solutions.title: Re-sum the window every time
solutions.idea: Store every reading and add up the last size of them on each call.

solutions.title: Ring buffer with a running sum
solutions.idea: One addition and at most one subtraction per reading. The slot about to be overwritten holds the reading that leaves the window.

followups: Readings come with timestamps, and the window is the last 60 seconds instead of the last k readings. What changes?
Report the median of the window instead of the mean. Which structure keeps that fast?
